symptom: ako/mxcli#866: "In a container restarted with the system cluster down, the `mxcli init` SessionStart hook runs `--ensure-db`, provisions a fresh **empty** cluster, and both apps boot healthy against it. Every captured row (7,966 laps here) is absent, and no error says so. An empty database is indistinguishable from a new one."
cause: `startLocalPostgres` fell back to the #823 user-owned initdb cluster whenever no service manager made the port ready, without asking whether a system cluster for that port existed; once #984 made that fallback actually work on Debian/Ubuntu, 'PostgreSQL is down' became 'PostgreSQL is empty'. Separately, the bootstrap hook's banner named the LAST log line containing 'error', which behind a service-manager diagnostic is pg_ctlcluster's own 'Error:' line, not mxcli's
file: `cmd/mxcli/docker/ensuredb.go` (`findSystemClusters`, `conflictingSystemCluster`, `systemClusterDownError`, `MXCLI_ENSURE_DB_NEW_CLUSTER`, the NEW-EMPTY warning in `startUserCluster`); `cmd/mxcli/init_hook.go` (banner takes the first `^Error:` line)
insight: The fallback's success was the defect: an empty database passes every check above it (role/db creation, boot, health), so the only place the difference is knowable is the moment before initdb — decide there, and announce every initdb loudly. Detect by data directory, not by service: Debian's /etc/postgresql/<v>/<n>/postgresql.conf is world-readable and carries the port, while the data dir is 0700 postgres, so a non-root stat of PG_VERSION returns EACCES — evidence OF a cluster; a probe that counts only err==nil misses exactly the devcontainer user. Match on port so an unrelated cluster never blocks, and treat an existing user-owned cluster as a restart (note the stopped system one, do not refuse). Measured on Ubuntu/PG16 with 16/main down, via a harness calling EnsureDatabase as a non-root user without sudo (privileges dropped in-process, since su was unavailable): fixed -> refusal naming /var/lib/postgresql/16/main; guard stubbed -> 'Database ready' on a new empty ~/.mxcli/postgres cluster, err nil. Trap that cost a cleanup: the first control binary predated the setuid step and ran as ROOT, whose `service postgresql start` succeeded and provisioned into the real cluster — print the uid in any privilege-sensitive harness before believing it. Hermeticity: the stub-PATH test helper must pin the probe root too; dev hosts (this one) have a stopped cluster on 5432
